questions.question: For a customer whose `city` is NULL, what do `CONCAT(name, ', ', city)` and `CONCAT_WS(', ', name, city)` return?
options: Both return the name followed by ', '
CONCAT returns NULL; CONCAT_WS returns just the name
CONCAT returns the name; CONCAT_WS returns NULL
questions.explanation: CONCAT returns NULL if any argument is NULL. CONCAT_WS skips NULL values after the separator, so it returns the name alone.

questions.question: Which filter for orders placed on 1 April 2025 can use an index on `created_at` for a range scan?
questions.explanation: Wrapping the column in a function makes the predicate non-sargable. A half-open range on the bare column lets the optimizer seek into the index.

questions.question: `created_at` is stored in UTC. Why might `CONVERT_TZ(created_at, 'UTC', 'Asia/Kolkata')` return NULL?
options: The MySQL time zone tables have not been loaded, so named zones are unknown
CONVERT_TZ only works on TIMESTAMP columns
CONVERT_TZ requires the session time_zone to be SYSTEM
questions.explanation: Named time zones require the tz tables populated via mysql_tzinfo_to_sql. Numeric offsets like '+05:30' work without them, and IST has no DST.

questions.question: What do `ROUND(1499.555, 2)` and `TRUNCATE(1499.555, 2)` return for this exact-value literal?
questions.explanation: For exact values ROUND rounds half away from zero, giving 1499.56. TRUNCATE simply drops the extra digits, giving 1499.55.
